classification.difficultyReason: Identify the gate diagonal as a hypotenuse, apply Pythagoras’ theorem and round to one decimal place.

inlines.text: A gate is 2.3 m wide with a height of 1.4 m.
Calculate the length of the diagonal of the gate correct to 1 decimal place.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5 gate illustration, lower-left of page
spec.description: Rectangular gate with two upright posts, vertical slats, horizontal rails and an outlined diagonal brace rising from bottom-left to top-right. Dimension arrows below and to the right retain dashed extension lines.
spec.mathematics: The diagonal spans a rectangle of width 2.3 m and height 1.4 m, forming the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied measurements are visible; the diagonal length is not supplied.

answer.worked:
The diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle.
$$\begin{align*}a^2+b^2&=h^2\\2.3^2+1.4^2&=h^2\\7.25&=h^2\\\sqrt{7.25}&=h\\h&\approx2.7\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
The diagonal is $2.7\text{ m}$, correct to 1 decimal place.
